newsitem.title: GREECE: Selonda makes waves with Italian stake.
newsitem.headline: Selonda makes waves with Italian stake.

text.p: Greece's Selonda Aquaculture is making waves in the fish farming industry with its latest acquisition of Trieste-based Marina & Maricolture Alto Adriatico SpA (MMAA).

Seeking to enlarge its production base, strengthen its market position and internationalise its activities, Selonda agreed to acquire a 40 percent stake in MMAA for 700 million drachmas through the latter's share capital increase.

"New dynamics are created in Mediterranean aquaculture and new perspectives for both groups after joining forces," company executives told a new conference at Duino Castle, a few kilometres outside Trieste in northern Italy.

MMAA was established in 1980. Like Selonda, which means blue wave in Catalan, it has been a pioneer in Mediterranean fish farming having contributed to the intensive culture of bass and bream in Italy.
Its founder, Domenico Baldini, a former "fish-exterminator" as he puts it, turned mussel breeder and soon developed a vision for marine aquaculture.

Today, along with son Lucio Baldini they run MMAA, a group with a large distribution network of fresh fish -- wild catch and farm grown -- with a packing, processing and distribution centre that puts out 300 tonnes of fish monthly.
The Selonda-MMAA group thus broadens its production base expecting 1997 output of 3,200 tonnes of fish with complementary size and season and more than 50 million fry.

"Synergies and the combined action of Maricolture with Eurofish, the export arm of the Selonda-Riopesca group, will reinforce our positioning in the Italian market which absorbs 60 percent of our sales," said Selonda chief executive John Stefanis.
Last year, MMAA completed installations of fish farming sites in off-shore floating cages in the gulf of Trieste and in the port of Budava in Croatia.

It also set up a modern processing, cold-storage facility for fish products in Villagio del Pescatore and expanded its hatchery in Monfalcone using the warm waste water from the nearby Enel power station.

The game plan now will capitalise on the geographic location of Maricolture's on-growing sites in the north Adriatic sea. Executives eye opportunities for a dynamic and cost effective penetration of central European markets like Austria and Germany.

"The enlarged group is becoming a major player in fry and fish production in Italy, Greece and the Mediterranean region. It is in a position to influence future developments in the aquaculture industry," Selonda's Stefanis said.

He told a news conference that the European Union's balance of trade in fishery products is in deficit. With total demand amounting to 9.0 million tonnes, EU landings of fish are around six million tonnes of which 1.4 million are exported.
Fish farming is only contributing 400,000 tonnes and the balance is satisfied by imports from other countries -- about 4.0 million tonnes valued at 8.0 billion ecu.

"With demand for seafood rising and supply from natural sources topping out, aquaculture is the only answer to providing the world with its seafood needs in the next century," Stefanis told the news conference at Duino castle.
